findings.message: ERQ-5 (docs/semester-1/gict-300/unit-02/unit-assessment.mdx:141-143) is an integrative evaluation of the "layered system" statement, while the approved blueprint words the integrative item as "requiring a hardware/software plan for a described school need" (specs/content/gict-300/content-spec.md:208-209). The plan demand is present in per-topic ERQ-1/2/4 and every structural constraint of the blueprint holds (5 ERQs, one per topic plus one integrative, Analyze to Evaluate, Analyse-or-higher rubric criteria); the owner may accept the delivered form or request a cycle-2 recast of ERQ-5.

The storage-hierarchy pyramid's registers and cloud rungs (docs/semester-1/gict-300/unit-02/topic-02.mdx:62-68 and fig-U2-3) are presented without citation and are not text-bound in the bound excerpt: the bourgeois2019 chapter 2 excerpt carries the RAM/disk speed-volatility core, not the full registers-to-cloud pyramid. The sources declaration's phrase "which the bound bourgeois2019 excerpt independently carries" (specs/content/gict-300/sources/unit-02.md, norton entry) is accurate for that core but generous for the full pyramid. Standard, uncontroversial content; no claim is attributed to an unverifiable source, so this does not fail sources.

docs/semester-1/gict-300/unit-02/topic-03.mdx:86-87 states Wallace and Clariana (2005) tested students "on exactly these concepts"; the bound excerpt supports "computer concepts that students are expected to master at the completion of an introductory computer fundamentals course" plus Excel skills, not exactly this unit's concept set. The numeric claims (60 percent below passing, about a third could exempt) are exactly supported. Soften "exactly" at the next content touch.

Further reading links use bare URLs as link text (e.g. topic-01.mdx:142, topic-02.mdx:144, topic-03.mdx:155, topic-04.mdx:141), reported as advisory by the render inspection; descriptive link text would serve screen-reader users better.

Unit-end ERQs 1-4 restate the four topic Summative task scenarios (digital corner, spending evaluation, staff-meeting explanation, remote-school network design). This is a deliberate rehearsal-then-assess design; no bound standard forbids it, but the unit-end items will partly measure recall of the rehearsed task rather than transfer. Recorded for owner awareness.

Concept-graph linkage looseness (specs/content/gict-300/concepts/unit-02.md): MCQ-08 (Linux open source) is listed under CON:GICT-300-2-11 "The boot sequence" (line 28) though the item exercises no boot knowledge; RRQ-05 under CON:GICT-300-2-10 (line 27) and RRQ-04 under CON:GICT-300-2-6 (line 23) are similarly weak. Governance-table data quality only; the concept-graph gate passes and no learner-facing content is affected.
